title: Cold rehydration cohort benchmarking and version compatibility manifest
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a reproducible offline benchmarking pipeline that measures cold KV cache rehydration behavior across model variants and sequence cohorts, and produce a machine-readable 'version compatibility manifest' used by onboarding and pinning tooling. Background: Current KV onboarding focuses on warm-cache steady-state metrics. We lack systematic microbenchmarks that simulate long-context cold starts and the resulting KV prefetch/rehydration costs for different model builds (float32, int8-quantized, continuous-batching tuned, etc.). This task will produce cohort definitions (context fingerprints grouped by token-distribution and role-type), run controlled rehydration traces against each model variant, and synthesize recommended compatibility levels for version pinning and fallback rules.
acceptance_criteria: Generate cohort taxonomy covering top 10K observed context fingerprints and produce at least 8 distinct cohort buckets (e.g., heavy-dialogue, short-instruction-rich, repeating-entity-longtail)
Run reproducible offline rehydration microbenchmarks for the top 50 models/variants and publish per-cohort p50/p95/p99 cold KV miss latency and memory working-set profiles to Grafana

Produce a version compatibility manifest (JSON) that maps model variants -> cohort suitability (allowed | recommended | incompatible) and store in model-registry with automated checksum and validation
Validate manifest accuracy by running a 72h canary simulation that predicts improvement in 95th tail latency for representative customer workload by at least 12% compared to baseline
tasks: Define context fingerprinting rules and cohort generation scripts (tokens, role markers, repeat-rate, entropy)
Implement offline rehydration runner that can simulate KV miss patterns and measure kernel-level latency and working set
Integrate runner with model-variant harness (v1 float32, v1-8bit, v2-quantized, runtime-optimized builds)
Collect traces from production sampling pipeline (1% sampling) and map to cohort buckets
Run full benchmark sweep and publish profiles to Grafana + model-registry
Author manifest schema and validation checks; add manifest publish step to onboarding CI
Create canary simulation harness and schedule 72h run on internal dedicated capacity
Write PRD and rollout runbook; coordinate with Solutions for Dedicated customers

notes_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: (1) Storing per-cohort prefetch indices reduces cold miss latency but increases registry size and onboarding time; (2) Conservative compatibility rules avoid regressions but limit rollout of new quantized builds; (3) More aggressive prefetching helps p95 but can increase memory pressure on Dedicated pools. Chosen approach favors a manifest that is permissive-recommended with an explicit 'storage_overhead' field so operators can opt-in per pool.
rollout_plan: Publish manifest for top 50 models to model-registry and mark as 'recommended' where simulation shows >=12% p95 improvement
Deploy read-only manifest to Hosted onboarding CI and run validation job — fail onboarding if 'incompatible'

If canary meets targets, set manifest to 'enforced' for new onboardings and document exceptions in runbook
